title: Unified Composite Endpoint PRD & Launch Playbook for Chat/Completion/Embeddings/Rerank
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: This PRD describes a Unified Composite Endpoint that lets customers submit a single request which simultaneously invokes chat/completion/embeddings/rerank behaviors and returns a combined structured response. Target users: platform engineers, product teams building RAG and multi-step pipelines, and partners that want a single-call experience with predictable latency and billing semantics. The goal is to ship a safe, observable, and cost-predictable composite surface that preserves existing single-endpoint contracts while enabling new multi-modal compositions and server-side orchestration. This document pairs requirements with a launch playbook and acceptance checklist.
scope: API: /v1/composite/execute - accepts a declarative composition payload describing steps (generate/embed/rerank/cond) and returns a JSON array of step outputs + unified metadata
Server-side orchestration: sequential and parallel step execution, optional KV prefix reuse, and token-level caching where applicable
Structured output and tool-calling compatibility for generate/chat steps
Billing and quota: per-step token and embedding accounting with consolidated invoice line items and clear per-step cost breakdown in Console
Per-model routing policy and fallback rules: customers can pin per-step model versions or allow runtime fallback to compatible variants
Observability: per-request trace id, per-step latency breakdown, token-level cost attribution, and dashboards in Redwood Console
out_of_scope: Server-side stateful sessions beyond KV cache (no long-lived session storage in v1)
Streaming responses that interleave outputs from multiple steps in a single HTTP chunk (streaming support planned in v2)
Making composite endpoint the default for existing single-endpoint SDK calls (explicit opt-in required)
On-prem private deployment advanced integrations that require kernel-level changes (deferred)
acceptance_criteria: Functional: The composite endpoint accepts a composition manifest and executes up to 8 steps within one request and returns result within the response schema defined in the API spec
Backward compatibility: Existing /v1/chat, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank endpoints continue to function with no behavioral changes
Performance: For standard small composition (2 steps: embed + rerank), p50 latency < 300ms and p95 latency < 900ms in hosted-us-west region under baseline load (25 RPS), with error rate < 0.2%
SLOs and error budget: Canary must show <50% of error budget consumption for 72h; ops runbook validated for fallback to single-step endpoints
Billing: Token and embedding cost per step is captured and shown in cost breakdown; invoice line items match telemetry and Console sample reports
Security: Request-level audit logging present for all composite calls and KMS-encrypted payloads for customers with require-encryption flag
Quality: Composite-led generation tests (100 synthetic prompts) must show no >10% degradation in semantic quality vs equivalent multi-call client orchestration measured by eval suite
Chaos/Failure modes: If any non-required step fails, composite returns partial results with errors per-step; if a required step fails, composite returns HTTP 5xx and triggers fallback policy
success_metrics: Adoption: 10 pilot customers onboarded within 8 weeks of GA
Cost-savings signal: Average tokens-per-result decreases by >=12% for pilot apps using server-side caching and batching vs client orchestration
Stability: Production error rate <=0.5% and platform incidents related to composite endpoint <=1 in first quarter
Latency: Mean p95 across pilot workloads within 20% of single-call baseline for equivalent end-to-end flows
rollout_plan: Internal alpha (Week 0-2): feature behind flag, internal Redwood integration tests and 3 internal apps exercise full manifest capabilities
Private beta (Week 3-6): 3-5 external pilot customers; enable detailed telemetry and cost reporting; require signed beta agreement
Canary (Week 7, 1 week): 0.5% production traffic routed with conservative resource limits and automated rollback on SLO breach
Gradual ramp (Week 8-12): increase to 5% then 25% with ongoing benchmarking and model routing validation
GA (Week 13): public docs, SDK support, Console UI for per-request breakdown, and standardized support SLAs
launch_checklist: API Spec: Finalized OpenAPI and example manifests (link: https://drive.redwood.ai/composite-apidoc) - owner: PM
SDKs: JS/Python SDKs updated with manifest builders and validation - owner: SDK
Runtime: ENG: orchestration worker, step isolation, prefix caching, and kernel compatibility tests merged (PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/472) - owner: ENG
Billing: Billing team verifies per-step accounting and Console displays sample invoice - owner: Billing Ops
Telemetry: Traces, step-level metrics, token accounting, and dashboards created (Dash link: https://dash.redwood.ai/composite) - owner: Observability
Security: Threat model review completed and audit logs enabled; KMS integration smoke tests passed - owner: Security
E2E Tests: Automated regression tests for step ordering, error propagation, and fallback behavior in CI - owner: QA
Performance: Load test report meeting p95 targets under expected traffic patterns (report link: https://perf.redwood.ai/reports/composite-v1) - owner: SRE
Docs: Quickstart, composition manifest guide, and migration guide from multi-call to composite - owner: DX
Support: Runbook and escalation path documented with sample Playbook for degraded mode - owner: Support
Legal/Commercial: Pricing addendum drafted for composite billing model and pilot contract templates - owner: RevOps
Launch comms: Blog draft, release notes, and changelog prepared - owner: Marketing
risks: Cost complexity: Per-step billing may confuse customers; need clear Console UI and examples
Performance tail latency: Orchestration across heterogeneous models can introduce tail amplification; mitigation: step-level timeouts and parallelism heuristics
Quality regressions: Server-side orchestration might produce different outputs vs client-side multi-call flows due to tokenization or model variant differences
Operational blast radius: New orchestration worker could introduce new failure domain; require staged rollout and conservative resource limits
mitigations: UI: Build per-request cost breakdown tab and billing preview in Console before GA
Timeouts/Retry: Default conservative per-step timeouts, idempotency tokens, and circuit-breaker for heavy steps
Quality monitoring: Eval hooks that compare composite vs reference multi-call outputs and trigger alerts on drift
Canary & Throttles: Auto-throttle composable requests at ingress to protect core serving runtime
open_questions: Should we allow streaming within a generate step in v1 if the overall composition includes other steps?
Exact canonical billing line item granularity: per-step vs per-request aggregated? (Finance decision required)
Do we permit cross-step KV reuse beyond prefix cache (e.g., shared context blobs) in v1?
What is the maximum recommended token budget per composite request before we reject with 413?
notes: We intentionally do not include streaming across steps in v1 to limit complexity and protect latency SLOs.
Pilot customers should be given a usage dashboard template and a cost-estimation worksheet.
Coordinate with Dedicated and Private teams to ensure model variant fallback contracts are respected across deployment modes.
